quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should generally:

options.text: Drive faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up. Turn on your signal, look for an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge safely.

questions.question: Drive below the speed limit when:

options.text: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
You see a police car.
You are entering a highway with other cars.
You are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road or weather conditions are not perfect.
questions.explanation: Slow down when roads are wet, slippery, or visibility is poor. Even at the posted speed limit, you can get a ticket for driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, you should:

options.text: Turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from.
Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.
Turn into the middle lane.
Turn into any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn into the lane closest to the lane you came from.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane that is closest to your previous lane. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: You may not park within ____ of a crosswalk.

options.text: 10 feet
20 feet
30 feet
40 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 20 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection. Park legally and make sure drivers can see your car from both directions.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels straight.
Leave your transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the curb when parking downhill. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: Stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your reaction time.
The time of day.
Your brakes' condition.
Your tires' condition and type.

questions.correctAnswerText: The time of day.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, weather, visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition, road conditions, and speed. Time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb:

options.text: Keep wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn wheels away from the curb.
Turn wheels toward the curb.
Turn back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels away from the curb when parking uphill. This prevents your car from rolling into traffic if your brakes fail.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.
Trucks are on the upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep hill or downgrade ahead.

questions.question: When should you return to your previous lane after passing?

options.text: When you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When the other vehicle signals you to return.
When you are directly next to the vehicle.
When you feel you are far enough ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Use your right turn signal before returning to your lane. Return when you can see the entire passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Car drivers should know that large trucks:

options.text: Have large blind spots.
Can stop faster than passenger vehicles.
Do not need more room to turn than passenger vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have large blind spots.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots in front, on the sides, and behind. Avoid these areas. Trucks need more room to turn and stop than passenger vehicles because of their size and weight.

questions.question: What traffic light means you must stop, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then go when the path is clear.

questions.question: When a school bus is stopped on the other side of a divided highway, what should drivers do?

options.text: May continue driving.
Must stop until the school bus begins moving.
Must stop until the stop arm is lifted.
Must stop and wait for the flashing lights to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: May continue driving.
questions.explanation: You can continue driving when a school bus is stopped on the other side of a divided highway. You only need to stop if the highway does not have a divider between the two directions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No passing zone.
Winding road.
Pedestrian crossing.
Low ground railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low ground railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a low ground railroad crossing. Railroad tracks cross the road at a steep angle. Low vehicles may scrape the bottom or get stuck on the tracks.

questions.question: What shape and color is a slow-moving vehicle emblem?

options.text: A rectangular red sign.
A circular green sign.
A diamond-shaped yellow sign.
A triangular orange sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A triangular orange sign.
questions.explanation: A slow-moving vehicle emblem is an orange reflective triangle. It warns that the vehicle is traveling 25 mph or slower.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic lanes going in opposite directions?

options.text: Yellow
White
Yellow and white
Yellow, white, and black

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. They are painted in the center of the road.

questions.question: When does your vehicle need more distance to stop?

options.text: On a wet or icy road.
On paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs more stopping distance on wet or icy roads. Loose gravel or stones also increase stopping distance.

questions.question: If your vehicle has Anti-Lock Brakes and starts to skid on a slippery road, what should you do?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Lightly tap the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Press down hard on the brake pedal and keep holding it while steering to safety. The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) automatically pumps the brakes faster than you can. Lifting off the pedal or pumping the brakes will turn off the ABS.

questions.question: What is used on some highways to show drivers which lanes to use for turning?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows show which lanes to use. They direct drivers to go straight or turn as needed.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when moving left, look:

options.text: Over your right shoulder.
At your side mirror.
Over your left shoulder.
At your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When should you NOT cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is disabled.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When doing so would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction of the arrow.
Come to a complete stop.
You may turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians pass.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. But oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians.

questions.question: What are highway signs called when they tell drivers they must follow an instruction?

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. If you do not follow them, you can be fined.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
Right after the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. This is because rain brings oil from the asphalt to the surface. Hot weather makes this worse.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Press your brakes hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Use your parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.

questions.question: When the road has a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line next to your lane, when may you pass?

options.text: Only in an emergency.
Only on an expressway.
If the road ahead is clear.
Only at an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: When you have a broken yellow line next to your lane and a solid line on the other side, you may cross to pass only if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road, you must:

options.text: Not cross the center line.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane meant for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane meant for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the oncoming lane to complete your pass. Only do this if it is safe and legal.

questions.question: If an oncoming car is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: Honk to get the other driver's attention. If they do not move, steer right to avoid them. Do not steer left because if the other driver moves at the last second, you will still crash. Brake firmly and steadily. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The safe speed limit for a residential area.
The safe speed limit for an expressway exit.
The safe speed limit for an expressway entrance.
The safe speed limit for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The safe speed limit for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the safe speed for leaving an expressway. In this example, the safe speed is 30 mph.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street in the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You may go if the way is clear.
You must come to a complete stop before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street in the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: If you pass these signs, you are going the wrong way and risk a head-on crash. Turn around carefully.

questions.question: What is the best way to stay safe when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Honk your horn right before you shift into reverse.
Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
Look in your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up your radio before backing up to alert people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before you get in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because drivers cannot see well behind their vehicles. Before you get in to back up, walk to the back of the vehicle and check for children and small objects.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. What must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
Demand the other vehicle pull over to make room.
Turn on your high beam headlights so the other vehicle sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, both vehicles need half the road to pass safely. Each driver must have enough space to pass without problems.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into a driveway or to exit a highway (where allowed).

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow arrow?

options.text: Merge in the direction the arrow is pointing.
Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Rely only on your mirrors.
Start signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before changing lanes on residential streets.
Always check your blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Other cars and motorcycles can hide in your blind spot. Always look over your shoulder before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before changing lanes on residential streets or 5 seconds before on freeways.

questions.question: What helps prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your emergency lights or horn when needed.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side as traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road where they can see traffic coming toward them.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It causes hearing loss.
It creates pollution.
It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
It causes poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases from the vehicle and keeps fumes out of the passenger area. Fix exhaust leaks right away to prevent carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.question: When you are in traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks completely without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross the tracks completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before entering the tracks, check that you have enough space to get completely across without stopping. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing any railroad tracks.

questions.question: Another driver is passing your car. What should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Signal to the other driver when it is safe to pass.
Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help them pass safely.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to help them pass safely.
questions.explanation: Stay to the right when another driver passes you on the left. Check for oncoming traffic and slow down slightly to let the passing vehicle merge back easily.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, what should you do?

options.text: Pass the vehicle on the right.
Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
Expect them to drive above the speed limit.
Follow closer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks carrying flammable liquids must stop at all railroad crossings. Be prepared to stop if you are following one of these vehicles.
